paragraphs: When used in this report, the terms "we," "us," "our," "BRCC," "Black Rifle Coffee," "Black Rifle Coffee Company," and the "Company" mean BRC Inc. and its consolidated subsidiaries, collectively, unless the context otherwise requires.

Black Rifle Coffee Company is a Veteran-founded and led premium coffee, and energy drink, company operating through one reportable segment composed of three primary channels: Wholesale, DTC, and Outposts. We leverage in-house media and content creation to support brand awareness, customer engagement, and community building. Founded in 2014 by U.S. Army Veteran Evan Hafer, Black Rifle Coffee began with a one-pound coffee roaster in a garage, where Hafer personally roasted, packaged, and shipped coffee directly to consumers. Today, we have grown into a widely recognized and nationally distributed brand steadfast in its commitment to supporting active-duty military, Veterans, first responders, and others who share our values.

Black Rifle Coffee operates out of offices in West Valley City, Utah; San Antonio, Texas; and Nashville, Tennessee, with a manufacturing facility in Manchester, Tennessee. Our product offerings have expanded beyond traditional roast coffee to include single-serve coffee and ready-to-drink coffee products, as well as Black Rifle Energy, a ready-to-drink energy beverage launched in late 2024. In addition, we offer Black Rifle branded apparel, coffee brewing equipment, and outdoor and lifestyle gear designed to extend brand engagement and customer loyalty.

Our mission at Black Rifle Coffee Company is to serve premium coffee and energy beverages and provide proprietary content to active-duty military, Veterans, first responders, and others who share our values. Founded and led by combat Veterans of the Global War on Terror, we are a mission-driven company committed to delivering quality products while giving back to the communities we serve. This dedication is reflected in our recruitment and hiring practices, charitable donations, and storytelling through our media channels.

As a public benefit corporation, Black Rifle Coffee Company balances profitability with purpose. Our public benefit purpose is to support active duty military members, Veterans, and first-responders, including underserved populations within those communities. We achieve this through objectives such as:
•Creating meaningful post-service career opportunities for Veterans, first responders, and their families.
•Supporting charities focused on mental health and other critical needs within these communities.
•Inspiring Veterans to pursue entrepreneurship through select programs and charitable support.
•Providing quality products and content that resonate with these audiences.

A significant factor in our success is the work ethic and discipline of our Veteran employees. We are committed to hiring Veterans and military spouses, supporting their transition from military service to private industry. This dedication fosters a strong, cohesive culture at Black Rifle Coffee Company, and we seek to maintain Veterans and military spouses as a meaningful portion of our workforce.

Our corporate giving is strengthened through direct cash and in-kind donations to charities aligned with our public benefit purpose, providing direct support to individuals, charities, and organizations aligned with our mission to serve those who serve.

We are a digitally native brand with an established omnichannel business model, operating through one reportable segment composed of three primary channels: Wholesale, DTC and Outposts. Each channel plays a distinct role in reaching our customers, building our community, and growing our brand.

In our Wholesale channel, we sell packaged coffee and our RTD beverages through leading Food, Drug, and Mass ("FDM") retailers such as Walmart, Sam's Club, regional and national grocery chains, and convenience stores, such as 7-Eleven, Casey's General Store, and Circle K. Additionally, our coffee, apparel, and gear are sold through specialty retailers like Bass Pro Shops, Scheels, and Ace Hardware. In 2025, the Wholesale channel generated $258.0 million in sales, compared to $245.0 million in 2024. We have prioritized growth in this channel by expanding distribution in grocery stores, club stores, convenience stores, and specialty retailers, positioning the Wholesale channel as a key driver of future revenue.

Our DTC platform has been the foundation of our business since the inception of the company and launch of www.blackriflecoffee.com. This channel enabled us to establish brand awareness and scale as a recognizable beverage brand in the United States. Through this channel, we engage directly with customers and obtain insight into consumer preferences. The DTC channel includes our subscription-based Coffee Club, through which customers can receive ground, whole bean, single-serve coffee, or apparel delivered to their home or office on a customizable schedule. As of December 31, 2025, the Coffee Club served approximately 159,900 active subscribers. In 2025, DTC sales totaled $117.6 million, compared to $123.8 million in 2024, reflecting a 5% decline primarily due to consumer purchasing behavior shifting toward retail channels and reallocation of resources in order to grow the Wholesale channel.

headings: Failure to maintain or enhance the value and reputation of our brand, including our support of the military, Veteran and first-responder communities, could have a negative impact on our financial results.
Our growth strategy depends on the successful execution of our strategic initiatives, and our limited operating history may make it difficult to evaluate future risks and challenges.
We have a limited operating history, and our past financial results may not be indicative of our future performance. Further, our revenue growth rate may slow as our business matures.
Our marketing programs may not be successful, resulting in harm to our financial results.
Our new products or merchandise may not generate increased sales or profits.
We are subject to risks associated with using social media as a primary form of advertisement and customer engagement.

Our current operations are highly dependent on the financial performance of our Wholesale and DTC channels, and reliance on third-party logistics, as well as other risks, could negatively impact our business.

Our profitability depends in part on successfully operating Outposts. We may be unsuccessful in opening or profitably operating new Outposts or establishing new markets, which could adversely affect our growth.
Failure to effectively manage growth could harm our business, financial condition and results of operations.
paragraphs: Risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from the results contemplated by the forward-looking statements contained in this Annual Report and other public statements we make are described below. Based on the information currently known to us, we believe that the matters discussed below identify the material risk factors affecting our business. However, the risks and uncertainties we face are not limited to those described below. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently believe to be immaterial, but that could later become material, may also adversely affect our business.

Our brand, including the quality of media content and active participation in the military, Veteran and first-responder communities, is core to our success, and damage to our brand or reputation and negative publicity could negatively impact our business, financial condition, and results of operations.

Our reputation and the quality of our brand are critical to our business and success in existing markets and will be critical to our success as we enter new markets. Our brand and authenticity in supporting the military, Veteran and first-responder communities is a core driver of our success. We promote our brand through media content and active participation in the military, Veteran and first-responder communities through events, donations, and hiring commitments, but the continued success of such promotions cannot be guaranteed.

We have historically faced, and may from time to time be faced, with negative publicity, regardless of its accuracy, relating to our brand; our founders and our mission; our charitable activities; our marketing; product quality; the safety, sanitation, and welfare of our facilities; customer complaints or litigation alleging illness or injury; health inspection scores; integrity of our or our suppliers' food processing, employment practices, and other policies, practices and procedures; employee relationships and welfare or other matters; or public statements by our founders or other key employees and persons associated with our brand, including paid brand partners. Negative publicity may adversely affect our business, regardless of its accuracy or whether we are ultimately found responsible.

Our brand has been in the past, and may be in the future, associated with controversial actions of certain customers of ours. For example, we have occasionally received negative publicity from leading national media arising out of the presence of, among others, our logos and brands on apparel worn at certain publicized events, even when such individuals were otherwise unaffiliated with us. The negative publicity and our reaction and communication related to such events has in the past resulted in losses to our DTC subscription service, the loss of investors, and the loss of Wholesale channel partners. There is no assurance that any such negative publicity will not occur again in the future and harm our brand and reputation, regardless of our involvement in the publicized events.

Moreover, social media platforms present additional risks, as they enable the rapid spread of information, including statements adverse to our interests, which may be inaccurate or misleading and could negatively impact our business, prospects, or financial performance. The potential harm from such content may be immediate and occur without affording us an opportunity for redress or correction. Our brand has been viewed as polarizing, which may subject us to boycotts, reputational harm, or other adverse actions by the public, investors, or entities that disagree with our mission or branding.

paragraphs: Unless the context otherwise requires, references to "we", "us", "our", "Black Rifle Coffee", "Black Rifle Coffee Company", "BRCC" and the "Company" in this section are to the business and operations of BRC Inc. and its consolidated subsidiaries. The following discussion and analysis should be read in conjunction with the audited annual consolidated financial statements and related notes thereto included in Part II, Item 8, Financial Statements and Supplementary Data of this Annual Report. In addition to historical information, this discussion contains forward-looking statements that involve risks, uncertainties, and assumptions that could cause BRCC's actual results to differ materially from management's expectations. Factors which could cause such differences are discussed herein and set forth in Part I, Item 1A, Risk Factors in this Annual Report.

Black Rifle Coffee Company is a Veteran-founded and led premium coffee, and energy drink company operating through one reportable segment composed of three primary channels: Wholesale, DTC, and Outposts. We leverage in-house media and content creation to support brand awareness, customer engagement, and community building. Founded in 2014 by U.S. Army Veteran Evan Hafer, Black Rifle Coffee began with a one-pound coffee roaster in a garage, where Mr. Hafer personally roasted, packaged, and shipped coffee directly to consumers. Today, we have grown into a widely recognized and nationally distributed brand steadfast in its commitment to supporting active-duty military, Veterans, first responders, and others who share our values.

In February 2022, we completed the Business Combination and as a result of the consummation of a series of mergers in connection therewith, Authentic Brands became a subsidiary of BRC Inc., with BRC Inc. acting as the sole managing member thereof as a public benefit corporation. The Business Combination was accounted for as a reverse acquisition and a recapitalization of Authentic Brands. Accordingly, the Business Combination was reflected as the equivalent of Authentic Brands issuing stock for the net assets of SilverBox, accompanied by a recapitalization. Under this method of accounting, SilverBox is treated as the "acquired" company for financial reporting purposes. The net assets of SilverBox are stated at historical cost, with no goodwill or other intangible assets recorded. This accounting treatment was determined by the controlling owner of Authentic Brands prior to the Business Combination, who also controls the combined company following the Business Combination.
Certain trends affecting our business within the respective sales channels are as follows:

•Wholesale channel revenue continues to increase as we add new customers and expand our presence in the FDM market. We expect continued revenue growth in this channel as we invest to increase brand awareness, and in customer acquisition, new product launches, including our Black Rifle Energy product line, and expanded distribution in the FDM market.

•DTC channel revenue decline has moderated as we continue to optimize customer acquisition, enhance retention, and provide our customers with a personalized and engaging shopping experience through targeted content and tailored product offerings on our website. Additionally, we are increasing our investment in major third-party ecommerce marketplaces in response to changing consumer purchasing behavior.

•Outpost channel revenue is stabilizing as we focus on improving transaction volumes and average order values through customer retention programs and tailored product offerings. In 2026, we expect limited growth in this channel as we reallocate investments to other channels while seeking to improve profitability through operational and strategic changes, which may include the closure of underperforming Outposts.

During the second quarter of 2025, management implemented the Operational Improvement Plan to reduce costs and improve the efficiency of certain company-wide functions. This plan was extended in the third and fourth quarters of 2025 as a result of the relocation of our corporate headquarters and a change in our third-party logistics provider. The cost of this plan was approximately $5.6 million consisting of severance and transition costs, substantially all of which were incurred as of December 31, 2025. We estimate that the costs savings as a result of this plan will exceed $8.9 million on an annualized run rate basis. As of December 31, 2025, we have realized approximately $5.3 million of these savings.

Maintaining and growing brand awareness and loyalty is critical to our success. We believe we have developed an effective marketing strategy that enhances brand awareness and drives consumer engagement. Consumer appreciation of our brand is primarily reflected in our sales across our three channels. We intend to continue to refine and develop our brand strategy utilizing reach-based formats such as streaming advertising and other select marketing channels. In addition, we will leverage our social media presence and employ targeted digital advertising to expand the reach of our brand.

We continue to expand our customer base through our Wholesale channel, with our products now available in a growing number of physical retail locations. Wholesale customers include large national retailers, regional retailers, distributors, and dealers, reflecting increased market presence and distribution reach.

We believe that consistently acquiring and retaining customers at a reasonable cost will be a key driver of our future performance. We continue to build brand awareness and reach new consumers by investing in existing and new channels and markets. Our capabilities in digital marketing and consumer engagement provide a competitive advantage in attracting, converting, and retaining our consumers. We remain focused on measuring and optimizing marketing performance to ensure that our advertising spend is efficient, while managing customer acquisition costs and maximizing returns on marketing investments.

We gain substantial economic value from repeat users of our products who consistently re-order our products. The pace of our growth rate may be affected by the repeat purchase behavior among existing and newly acquired customers.

Our goal is to continue to expand our product line over time to increase our growth opportunities and reduce product-specific risks through diversification into multiple products intended for regular consumer use. Our pace of growth will be partially affected by the timing and scale of new product launches. We believe that it is important to our business to continue to innovate with new products and flavors.

Our ability to grow and meet future demand will be affected by our ability to properly plan for and source inventory from a variety of suppliers and co-manufacturers located inside and outside the United States. The majority of our green coffee beans come from Colombia, Brazil, and Nicaragua and since 2020, we have also sourced green coffee beans from more than ten additional countries in Latin America, Africa, and Asia to diversify our supply chain and offer our customers specialty and limited-time-only roasts. Quality control is a critical component of our manufacturing and supply chain operations. All of our bagged coffee is roasted in the United States. Our licensed, Coffee Quality Institute-certified grader and former Green Beret, oversees cupping, grading, scoring, and sourcing of our coffees. We also must effectively manage our co-manufacturers and suppliers.

paragraphs: 當本報告中使用 "we," "us," "our," "BRCC," "Black Rifle Coffee," "Black Rifle Coffee Company," 以及 "Company" 這些詞語時，係指 BRC Inc. 及其合併子公司， collectively，除非文意另有要求。

Black Rifle Coffee Company 是一家由退伍軍人創辦並領導的高階咖啡與能量飲料公司，透過一個應報告分部運作，該分部由三個主要通路組成： Wholesale、DTC 以及 Outposts。我們利用內建的媒體與內容創作來支持品牌知名度、客戶參與及社羣建立。Black Rifle Coffee 於 2014 年由美國陸軍退伍軍人 Evan Hafer 創辦，最初僅是一個在車庫內的咖啡烘焙機，Hafer 本人親自烘焙、包裝並直接將咖啡寄送給消費者。目前，我們已成長為一個廣為認知且全國性分銷的品牌，堅定支持現役軍人、退伍軍人、第一 responders 及其他與我們價值觀相符的人士。

Black Rifle Coffee 的辦公室位於美國猶他州西瓦利城、德克薩斯州聖安東尼奧以及田納西州納什維爾，並在田納西州曼徹斯特設有製造廠。我們的產品線已從傳統烘焙咖啡擴展至單人份咖啡與即飲咖啡產品，以及 Black Rifle Energy，這是一款於 2024 年年底推出的即飲能量飲料。此外，我們也提供 Black Rifle 品牌的服飾、咖啡沖煮設備以及戶外與生活方式用品，以延續品牌參與度與客戶忠誠度。
我們在 Black Rifle Coffee Company 的使命是提供高階咖啡與能量飲料，並為現役軍人、退伍軍人、第一 responders 及其他與我們價值觀相符的人士提供專屬內容。由全球反恐戰爭中的戰鬥退伍軍人創辦並領導，我們是一家以使命為導向的公司，致力於提供高品質產品，同時回饋我們服務的社區。這種承諾體現在我們的招聘與僱用實踐、慈善捐贈以及透過媒體頻道的敘事中。
作為一家公共利益公司，Black Rifle Coffee Company 優化利潤與使命的平衡。我們的公共利益使命是支持現役軍人、退伍軍人與第一 responders，包括這些社區內的弱勢羣體。我們透過以下目標來實現此使命：
•為退伍軍人、第一 responders 及其家庭創造有意義的退伍後職業機會。
•支持專注於心理健康及其他這些社區關鍵需求的慈善機構。
•透過特定計畫與慈善支持，激勵退伍軍人追求創業。
• 提供符合這些受眾喜好的高品質產品與內容。
我們成功的重要因素之一，是 Veteran 員工的工讀精神與紀律。我們致力於聘僱 Veteran 與軍人配偶，協助他們從軍事服務轉型至民間產業。這份承諾促成了 Black Rifle Coffee Company 強而有凝聚力的文化，我們致力於維持 Veteran 與軍人配偶在員工中佔有有意義的比例。
我們的企業捐贈透過直接現金與實質捐贈至與我們公共利益目的相符的慈善機構，提供直接支持給與我們使命相符的個人、慈善機構與組織，即服務那些服務者。
我們是一個數位原生品牌，擁有已建立的全通路商業模式，透過一個應報告分部運作，該分部由三個主要通路組成： Wholesale、DTC 與 Outposts。每個通路在接觸客戶、建立社羣與拓展品牌上扮演獨特的角色。

在 Wholesale 通路中，我們透過領導的 Food, Drug, and Mass（"FDM"）零售商，如 Walmart、Sam's Club、區域與全國性零售連鎖店，以及便利商店，如 7-Eleven、Casey's General Store 與 Circle K，銷售包裝咖啡與我們的 RTD 飲料。此外，我們的咖啡、服飾與裝備也透過專業零售商店如 Bass Pro Shops、Scheels 與 Ace Hardware 銷售。2025 年，Wholesale 通路產生 258.0 百萬美元銷售額，與 2024 年的 245.0 百萬美元相比。我們已優先推動此通路的成長，透過擴大在零售商店、俱樂部商店、便利商店與專業零售商店的通路，將 Wholesale 通路定位為未來營收的重要驅動力。

我們的 DTC 平台自公司成立與 www.blackriflecoffee.com 開通以來，一直是我們業務的基礎。此通路使我們得以建立品牌知名度，並在美國成為可辨識的飲料品牌。透過此通路，我們直接與客戶互動，並獲取消費者偏好資訊。DTC 通路包含我們的訂閱式 Coffee Club，客戶可透過此服務定期收到研磨咖啡、整豆咖啡、單次使用咖啡或服飾，按自訂時程送至家中或辦公室。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，Coffee Club 約有 159,900 名活躍訂閱者。2025 年 DTC 銷售總計為 117.6 百萬美元，與 2024 年的 123.8 百萬美元相比，下降 5%，主要因消費者購買新趨向零售通路，並重新配置資源以成長 Wholesale 通路。

paragraphs: 除非文意另有所指，否則本節所提及的「we」、「us」、「our」、「Black Rifle Coffee」、「Black Rifle Coffee Company」、「BRCC」及「the Company」均指 BRC Inc. 及其合併子公司之業務與運作。以下討論與分析應與本年度報告第二部分，第 8 項「財務報表與補充資料」所載之經審計年度合併財務報表及其相關附註一併閱讀。除歷史資訊外，本討論包含前瞻性陳述，涉及風險、不確定性與假設，這些因素可能導致 BRCC 實際結果與管理階層預期有重大差異。導致此等差異的因素於本節及第一部分，第 1A 項「風險因素」中已討論並列示。

Black Rifle Coffee Company 為由退伍軍人創辦與領導的高階咖啡與能量飲料公司，透過一個應報告分部運作，該分部包含三個主要通路： Wholesale、DTC 與 Outposts。我們利用內建媒體與內容創作來支持品牌認知度、客戶參與與社羣建設。Black Rifle Coffee 於 2014 年由美國陸軍退伍軍人 Evan Hafer 創立，最初僅以車庫內的一磅咖啡烘焙機開始，Hafer 先生親自烘焙、包裝並直接將咖啡送至消費者手中。如今，我們已成長為一個廣為認可且全國性分銷的品牌，堅定支持現役軍人、退伍軍人、第一 responders 及其他與我們價值觀相符的人士。

我們於 2022 年 2 月完成業務合併，並因完成一系列與此相關的合併，Authentic Brands 成為 BRC Inc. 的子公司，BRC Inc. 作為其唯一的管理成員，以公共利益公司形式運作。此業務合併被視為一項反向收購及 Authentic Brands 的資本結構重組。因此，此業務合併被視為 Authentic Brands 發行股票換取 SilverBox 的淨資產，並伴隨資本結構重組。根據此會計方法，SilverBox 被視為「被收購」公司，用於財務報告目的。SilverBox 的淨資產以歷史成本列示，不計入任何商譽或其他無形資產。此會計處理方式由 Authentic Brands 在業務合併前的控制權所有者所決定，該所有者亦在業務合併後繼續控制合併後的公司。
影響我們在各銷售通路業務的一些趨勢如下：
• Wholesale 通路的營業收入持續增加，因我們增加新客戶並擴大在 FDM 市場的佔有率。我們預期此通路的營業收入將持續成長，因我們投資以提高品牌認知度、客戶獲取、新產品發佈，包括我們的 Black Rifle Energy 產品線，以及在 FDM 市場的擴大分銷。
• DTC 通路的營業收入下滑已趨緩，因我們持續優化客戶獲取、提高留存率，並透過網站上的定向內容與個性化產品選擇，為客戶提供個性化且互動的購物體驗。此外，我們也增加在主要第三方電商市場的投資，以回應消費者的購買新趨勢。
• Outposts 通路的營業收入已趨於穩定，因我們專注於透過客戶留存計畫與個性化產品選擇提高交易金額與平均訂單價值。我們預期在 2026 年，此通路的成長將有限，因我們重新配置投資至其他通路，同時尋求透過運營與戰略變革提高利潤率，這可能包括關閉表現不佳的 Outposts。

在 2025 年第二季，管理階層實施運營改善計畫以降低成本並提高某些公司-wide 功能的效率。此計畫因公司總部遷移及第三方物流供應商變更，於 2025 年第三及第四季延長。此計畫的成本約為 5.6 百萬美元，包含遣散費與過渡費用，幾乎全部於 2025 年 12 月 31 日前產生。我們估計此計畫所帶來的成本節省，按年化運行率計算，將超過 8.9 百萬美元。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們已實現約 5.3 百萬美元的成本節省。
維持並提升品牌知名度與忠誠度對我們的成功至關重要。我們認為我們已經發展出一套有效的行銷策略，能提升品牌知名度並促進消費者參與。消費者對我們品牌的認可主要反映在我們三個通路的銷售表現上。我們有意繼續完善與發展品牌策略，利用基於觸達率的格式，例如串流廣告及其他選擇性行銷通路。此外，我們將善用我們的社交媒體存在，並運用針對性的數位廣告來擴大品牌的觸達範圍。
我們持續透過 Wholesale 通路擴大客戶羣，目前我們的產品已於越來越多的實體零售據點販售。Wholesale 客戶包括大型全國性零售商、區域性零售商、經銷商與經銷商，反映我們市場存在與分銷觸達範圍的增加。
我們認為持續以合理成本取得並留住客戶將是我們未來表現的關鍵驅動因素。我們持續透過投資現有與新興的通路與市場來建立品牌知名度並觸達新消費者。我們在數位行銷與消費者參與方面的能力，為吸引、轉化與留住消費者提供了競爭優勢。我們持續專注於衡量與優化行銷表現，以確保我們的廣告支出具備效率，同時管理客戶取得成本並最大化行銷投資回報。
我們從產品的重複使用者身上獲得顯著的經濟價值，這些使用者持續重複訂購我們的產品。我們的成長速度可能受到現有與新取得客戶重複購買行為的影響。
我們的目標是持續擴充產品線，以增加成長機會並透過多元化進入手多種產品，降低產品特定風險，這些產品是為常規消費者使用所設計。我們的成長速度將部分受到新產品發佈的時機與規模的影響。我們認為持續以新產品與新口味創新對我們的業務至關重要。

我們能否成長並滿足未來需求，將受到我們能否妥善規劃並從多種供應商與共同製造商（位於美國境內與境外）取得存貨的影響。我們絕大多數的綠咖啡豆來自哥倫比亞、巴西與尼加拉瓜，自 2020 年起，我們也從拉丁美洲、非洲與亞洲超過十個國家取得綠咖啡豆，以多元化我們的供應鏈並為客戶提供特調與限定時限定烘焙的產品。品質控制是我們製造與供應鏈運作的關鍵零組件。我們所有的包裝咖啡均在美國烘焙。我們的經授權、Coffee Quality Institute 認證的評級員與前 Green Beret，負責 oversee 我們咖啡的評鑑、評級、評分與來源。我們也必須有效地管理我們的共同製造商與供應商。

headings: 與我們業務相關的風險
未能維持或提升我們品牌的價值與聲譽，包括我們對軍事、退伍軍人及第一 responders 社羣的支持，可能會對我們的財務結果產生負面影響。
我們的成長策略依賴於我們戰略方案的成功執行，而我們有限的營運歷史可能使我們難以評估未來的風險與挑戰。
我們有有限的營運歷史，我們過去的財務結果可能無法反映我們未來的表現。此外，隨著我們業務成熟，我們的收入成長率可能減緩。
我們的行銷方案可能無法成功，導致對我們財務結果造成損害。
我們的新產品或商品可能無法產生更高的銷售額或利潤。
我們面臨使用社交媒體作為主要廣告與客戶互動形式相關的風險。
我們目前的營運高度依賴 Wholesale 和 DTC 頻道的財務表現，以及對第三方物流的依賴，以及其他風險，可能會對我們的業務產生負面影響。
本公司之獲利能力部分取決於成功運作 Outposts。我們可能無法成功開設或獲利運作新 Outposts 或建立新市場，這可能會對本公司之成長造成不利影響。
若無法有效管理成長，可能會損害本公司之業務、財務狀況及營運成果。
paragraphs: 可能導致我們實際結果與本年度報告及其他公開聲明中所預期的結果有重大差異的風險與不確定性，請參閱下文說明。根據目前我們所知的資訊，我們認為下文所討論的項目已識別出影響我們業務的關鍵風險因素。然而，我們所面臨的風險與不確定性並不限於下文所述。此外，尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前我們尚未知悉，或目前認為不重要，但未來可能變得重要，也可能對我們的業務產生不利影響。
我們的品牌，包括媒體內容的品質與在軍事、退伍軍人及第一 responders 社羣的積極參與，是我們成功的核心，若我們的品牌或聲譽受損，或出現負面宣傳，可能會對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運結果產生負面影響。
我們的聲譽與品牌品質對我們的業務及在現有市場的成功至關重要，並在我們進入新市場時同樣至關重要。我們在支持軍事、退伍軍人及第一 responders 社羣方面的品牌與真實性，是我們成功的核心驅動力。我們透過媒體內容與在軍事、退伍軍人及第一 responders 社羣的活動、捐贈與僱用承諾來推廣品牌，但這些推廣活動的持續成功無法保證。
我們過去曾面臨，且有時仍會面臨與我們品牌、創始人與我們的使命、慈善活動、行銷、產品品質、我們設施的安全、衛生與員工福利、客戶投訴或聲稱導致疾病或傷害的法律訴訟、健康檢查分數、我們或我們供應商的食品加工過程的誠信、就業實務及其他政策、實務與程序、員工關係與福利或其他事項的負面宣傳，無論這些宣傳是否準確。負面宣傳可能會對我們的業務產生不利影響，無論其是否準確或我們最終是否被判定負責任。

我們的品牌過去曾與某些客戶的爭議性行為有所關聯，未來也可能如此。例如，我們偶爾會因某些公開活動中出現我們的標誌與品牌而收到主要全國媒體的負面報導，即使這些個人與我們毫無關聯。過去，負面報導與我們對這些事件的反應與溝通，導致我們的 DTC 訂閱服務損失、投資者流失與 Wholesale 頻道合作夥伴流失。無法保證未來不會再次出現類似負面報導，並對我們的品牌與聲譽造成傷害，無論我們是否參與這些公開事件。
此外，社交媒體平台也帶來額外風險，因為它們能迅速散佈資訊，包括對我們不利的陳述，這些資訊可能不正確或誤導性，並可能對我們的業務、前景或財務表現產生負面影響。這種內容可能立即造成傷害，且我們可能沒有機會進行糾正或反駁。我們的品牌被視為具有兩極化色彩，這可能使我們面臨公眾、投資者或與我們使命或品牌定位意見不合的機構的罷買、聲譽損害或其他不利行動。
